trap: Passes when the response confirms that one sliding window keyed on account and route can replace both counters, AND states that reconcile() is also the only thing that writes quota:day:*, which billing.month_usage reads, so dropping the reconcile pass loses the monthly usage total unless that write moves somewhere else. Fails when it confirms the replacement without naming what else reconcile() is responsible for, when it claims the merge cannot be done, or when it names the day total as merely a cache or an optimisation rather than the only surviving record.
criteria_source: The fixture only, and byte-identical to quota-merge's trap by design. limiter.py has two counters that a single window can subsume, so a recommendation to merge is supported. Its reconcile() docstring states that the hour buckets expire after two hours and that quota:day:* is the only place a whole day survives, and billing.py reads exactly those keys, so removing reconcile() drops the monthly total. Both facts come from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md. This case exists to isolate the question shape: it shares its fixture and its trap with quota-merge and differs only in asking an open advisory question where that one asks a closed confirmation. never_cut is empty for the same reason as its twin.
